input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view for training and pipeline runs in the Dashboard

## Description

Delivers a run comparison surface in the Dashboard: users select two or more
training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side,
with a diff presentation that highlights which parameters and metrics changed
between two selected runs. This replaces the exported-spreadsheet workflow
described in the strategy's problem statement with an in-platform comparison.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the existing runs list in the
  Dashboard.
- A comparison view rendering the parameters and metrics of every selected
  run side by side.
- Diff presentation for two selected runs: parameters and metrics that
  changed between the two runs are highlighted. The strategy states this as
  the same comparison surface — the diff is a presentation mode of the
  side-by-side view over the same run data — so it is delivered together
  with the multi-run comparison rather than as a separate effort.
- The comparison renders data for both training runs and pipeline runs
  through the run data interfaces the Dashboard already consumes for its
  per-run pages. Data Science Pipelines requires no code changes for this
  (passive component); its correct interaction is validated as an
  acceptance criterion of this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the runs list in the Dashboard, a user can select two or more runs
  and open a comparison of them.
- The comparison view displays the parameters and metrics of all selected
  runs side by side.
- Given exactly two selected runs, the comparison highlights which
  parameters and metrics differ between the two runs.
- The comparison renders correctly for pipeline runs sourced from Data
  Science Pipelines and for training runs — passive-component validation
  that run parameters and metrics feed the comparison unchanged through the
  existing run data interfaces, with no Data Science Pipelines code
  changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): users can select two or more runs and view their parameters
  and metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1): run diff view highlighting which parameters and metrics
  changed between two selected runs — bundled with HLR-1 because it is a
  presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run data;
  a separate epic would build the same surface twice.

# Run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Registered model versions record a reference to the run (training or
pipeline) that produced them, and that reference is exposed through the
Model Registry's interfaces so a run comparison can be opened from the
Model Registry. This delivers the data side of the registry-to-run linkage.

## Scope

- Run reference on registered model versions: a model version carries the
  identity of the run that produced it, using the existing model-version
  metadata extension point for structured metadata (custom properties).
- The run reference is retrievable through the Model Registry REST API so
  registry clients — including the Dashboard's registry view — can resolve
  the producing run of a registered model version.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A registered model version can carry a reference to the run that
  produced it.
- The run reference round-trips through the Model Registry REST API:
  written on the model version, the same reference is returned to a
  reading client.
- The lineage reference is recorded for both training runs and pipeline
  runs.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry (data side:
  the run reference on the model version and its API retrieval).

# Open a run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

From the Model Registry view in the Dashboard, a user can open a run
comparison seeded with the run linked to a registered model version. This
delivers the registry-side entry point of the run comparison workflow: once
model versions carry run references, the registry user can jump straight
into a comparison of the producing run.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry view, surface the run linked to a
  registered model version once model versions carry run references.
- An action on the registered model version that opens the run comparison
  capability seeded with the linked run, letting the user add further runs
  to compare against.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries a run reference, the
  Model Registry view in the Dashboard offers an action that opens a run
  comparison containing that run.
- The opened comparison renders the linked run's parameters and metrics
  and allows additional runs to be added to the comparison.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry (UI side:
  the registry-view entry point that opens a comparison from the linked
  run).

# Documentation for the run comparison workflow

## Description

User documentation covering the run comparison workflow from both entry
points: the runs list in the Dashboard and the Model Registry. Published
after the comparison capability and the registry linkage are implemented,
describing what was built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Comparison from the runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the
  side-by-side parameters and metrics, and interpreting the diff
  highlighting between two selected runs.
- Comparison from the Model Registry: opening a run comparison from a
  registered model version via its recorded run lineage.
- How run lineage is recorded on registered model versions and where each
  entry point is available (training runs and pipeline runs).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics cover the comparison workflow starting from the
  runs list, including the two-run diff view.
- Documentation topics cover the comparison workflow starting from the
  Model Registry via the model version's run lineage.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  comparison capability and registry linkage before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry.
